blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Video dubbing aims to synthesize lip movements that match target speech while preserving the speaker identity, head pose, and background of a source video. Existing editors are predominantly trained via self-reconstruction under original paired audio, even though the source mouth becomes a conflicting target when driving speech is replaced. We introduce replacement-aware cross-audio supervision: paired-audio samples use full-frame reconstruction, whereas unpaired replacement-audio samples mask out source-mouth reconstruction losses and supervise the mouth solely through audio-visual synchronization while preserving unmasked facial regions and background. Because offline dubbing provides the complete source video and target speech beforehand, we present VidDub, a full-context diffusion editor distilled into two denoising steps (2 NFE). Our replacement-aware teacher first learns accurate lip synchronization without regressing toward conflicting source mouth movements. Matched trajectory regression then transfers the teacher's CFG-guided trajectories to a two-step student, and distribution matching distillation recovers visual quality after step compression. We will release the curated training dataset, VidDub-Bench, fixed paired- and cross-audio evaluation manifests, preprocessing outputs, and unified evaluation code. Across three training seeds, masking out conflicting source-mouth reconstruction improves cross-audio Sync-C by 0.833; the final two-step model combines strong lip synchronization with superior visual quality, identity preservation, and visual speech recognition across four benchmarks.
blocks.zh: 视频配音旨在合成与目标演讲相匹配的口语动作, 现有的编辑人员主要通过在原配对音频下进行自建来进行训练,尽管在驾驶语音被替换时源口成为相冲突的目标. 我们引入了重置意识跨音频监督:配对-音频样本采用全帧重建,而未配对的重置-音频样本掩盖了源口重建损失,仅通过视听同步来监督口腔,同时保留了未蒙面的面部区域和背景. 因为离线配音提前提供了完整的源视频和目标演讲,所以我们呈现出VidDub,一个完整的通则传播编辑器蒸馏出两个去诺化步骤(2个NFE). 我们的替代意识老师首先学会准确的口语同步,而不向相冲突的源口运动倒退. 相匹配的轨迹回归后再将老师的CFG制导轨迹转移给双步生,分布相匹配的蒸馏在相继压缩后会恢复视觉质量. 我们将公布经整理的培训数据集VidDub-Bench、固定对接和跨音频评价清单、预处理产出和统一评价代码。 在三个培训种子中,掩盖相互冲突的源口重建使跨声道Sync-C改进了0.833;最后的两步模式结合了强口同步与优异视觉质量,身份保存,视觉语音识别四个基准.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Video dubbing synthesizes lip movements that match replacement speech while
preserving the speaker identity, head motion, and scene of a source video.
Feed-forward and inpainting-based editors [ 31 , 5 , 56 ] and
recent latent-space and diffusion-based editors [ 28 , 55 , 21 , 30 ] have substantially improved visual
fidelity, while few-step distillation reduces iterative sampling cost [ 34 , 37 , 24 , 50 , 49 ] . However, their primary
training objective remains same-audio self-reconstruction: the model receives the
original paired speech and is supervised to reproduce the mouth motion already
present in the source video. This objective does not directly match the test-time
task of dubbing, which requires replacing mouth articulation under new speech while
leaving all other visual content unchanged.

blocks.en:
The core challenge lies in the supervision conflict between same-audio
reconstruction and cross-audio dubbing. Under original paired speech, the source
mouth, identity, pose, and background all serve as consistent ground-truth targets.
Under unpaired replacement speech, the source mouth articulates different content
and directly conflicts with the target audio, whereas the unmasked face and
background remain valid ground truth. Standard reconstruction losses do not
distinguish between these two regimes, and few-step distillation cannot recover
accurate cross-audio lip synchronization if the teacher is penalized for deviating
from the source mouth. Moreover, evaluation protocols centered on short same-audio
clips fail to expose this discrepancy. We therefore study how to train cross-audio
lip synchronization without target conflict, distill the resulting model into two
denoising steps, and evaluate it systematically across video domains and durations.

blocks.en:
We propose VidDub, starting with replacement-aware cross-audio supervision .
For paired same-audio samples, we apply standard full-frame reconstruction losses.
For unpaired replacement-audio samples, we mask out flow-matching, pixel, and
perceptual reconstruction losses inside the mouth region, preserve the unmasked face
and background via spatial reconstruction, and supervise mouth articulation with an
audio–visual synchronization loss. This decoupled formulation turns cross-audio
dubbing into a well-posed local editing task: target speech drives lip articulation,
while the source video anchors identity, head pose, and background.

blocks.en:
Long videos are processed using overlapping 81-frame windows conditioned on the
corresponding source frames. Each window uses two denoising steps; consecutive
windows advance by 64 frames and blend the 17-frame overlap. This sliding-window
scheme bounds computation and memory while retaining bidirectional context within
each window.

窗口由64个帧推进,并混合了17个帧的重叠。 这个滑倒的窗口
方案限制计算和内存,同时保留双向上下文
每个窗口。

blocks.en:
Relation to causal few-step methods. Lip Forcing [ 6 ] represents the causal two-step design paradigm, and
Causal Forcing develops causal ODE/DMD objectives [ 60 , 58 ] . Our controlled same-backbone comparison shows
that causal attention reduces first-frame latency but does not improve offline
throughput or output quality. VidDub therefore combines replacement-aware
cross-audio supervision with direct full-context distillation.

* 因果关注减少了第一个框架的延迟,但没有改善离线
产量或产出质量。 因此,VidDub结合了替换意识
使用直接的全文分解来进行跨音频监督.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We presented VidDub, a full-context two-step dubbing model built on
replacement-aware cross-audio supervision. For unpaired replacement speech, it
masks source-mouth reconstruction while retaining non-mouth reconstruction and
target-audio synchronization. Full-context trajectory regression transfers the
teacher to two denoising steps, and distribution matching improves visual quality.
Across four source domains, VidDub combines accurate replacement-speech
articulation with identity preservation and stable minute-long generation.

blocks.en:
This completed study evaluates the final full-context VidDub model.
Fifteen bilingual participants each completed all 150 anonymized A/B trials covering
50 generated sources and three opponents. Each trial asks which video is
better in lip synchronization, mouth realism, identity preservation, temporal
stability, and overall quality. Left/right assignment and the order of the first
four criteria are randomized; overall quality is always shown last. The interface
exposes neither method identity nor metrics. Table 49 reports VidDub/opponent/tie outcomes for each opponent and criterion, with ties
retained.

blocks.en: Appendix O Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 附录O 道德考虑

blocks.en:
High-fidelity lip synchronization can support translation, accessibility, and
post-production, but can also facilitate impersonation and misattributed speech.
VidDub edits a source video and can make a real person appear to say words they
never said. We use
only public research benchmarks and generated H3 subjects for figures; no private
recordings of identifiable people are released. We will not redistribute source
media whose licenses or consent basis do not permit redistribution, and will publish
a dataset/model card documenting provenance, permitted use, and a removal-request
channel before releasing artifacts. Model access will require a use agreement
forbidding non-consensual impersonation; released outputs will include provenance
metadata, and detector baselines will accompany the model. The blinded human study uses only generated H3
subjects, so no real person’s likeness is edited for it; raters are adult volunteers who
may stop at any time, and nothing beyond an anonymous rater ID is stored.
